subject: LumosBank - auditline export SLAs and incremental slice delivery
messages:
From: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@lumosbank.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Liao <james.liao@lumosbank.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Auditline export: SLA for slices & incremental handoff

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — the team liked the latency guarantees and the KV caching approach. As we prepare the RFP scoring, we need a clearer picture of your auditline export capabilities. Two specific asks from our security and e-discovery teams:

1) Incremental slice delivery: we need an approach for delivering daily delta slices (per-tenant) for a 24-month window. We care about sequence continuity and tamper evidence.
2) Export formats & transport: support for compressed ndjson, CSV manifest, and SFTP/S3 delivery with presigned URLs; preference is S3 presigned.

Could you provide:
- Proposed SLA for delivering slice bundles after the slice window closes (e.g., 24 hours, 72 hours)
- Evidence primitives for integrity (HMACs, signed manifests, monotonic sequence IDs)
- A sample timeline for a one-time bulk handoff vs ongoing daily slices

Also attaching our trimmed question set (lumos_rfp_questions_q3_v2.pdf). Can we aim to have a written reply early next week?

Best,

Sara Thompson
Director, Information Security
LumosBank

---
Attachment: lumos_rfp_questions_q3_v2.pdf (pdf, 132KB)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@lumosbank.com>
Cc: James Liao <james.liao@lumosbank.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Auditline export: SLA for slices & incremental handoff

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear asks and the doc. Short answers up front, then a concise plan below.

TL;DR:
- SLA (daily incremental slices): 24–48 hours post-window for S3 presigned delivery (standard tier); 72 hours for SFTP transfers.
- Integrity/evidence: signed manifest + SHA256 HMAC per bundle; monotonic slice_seq_id and per-record offsets; optional COSE signatures for high-assurance customers.
- Bulk handoff: we can stage a full 24-month harvest within 7 business days (dependent on data volume and redaction requirements).

Planned deliverables (proposal):
1) Daily delta slice workflow:
   - Slice generation at 00:00 UTC for previous UTC day.
   - Processing window: 0–6 hours for extract & dedup (adaptive by workload).
   - Delivery SLA: presigned S3 + signed manifest available within 24–48 hours. Manifest contains bundle_id, slice_seq_id, start/end timestamps, and HMAC(SHA256) over concatenated file checksums.
2) Tamper evidence:
   - Each bundle includes: bundle.ndjson.gz, bundle.manifest.json, bundle.signature.cose (optional).
   - Manifest fields: monotonic sequence, ingest cursor, bundle hash, producer timestamp, signature. We provide verification tool (python script) in the handoff package.
3) Bulk handoff vs ongoing:
   - Bulk (one-time): snapshot export pipeline, incremental indexing, and manifest chain. Estimated baseline: 3–7 business days for 500GB–2TB range; parallelization can shorten windows.
   - Ongoing: continuous daily slices with retention metadata and lifecycle tagging.

I attached a short spreadsheet with a sample cadence and file schema mapping (redwood_audit_export_proposal_v1.xlsx). Can we schedule a 30-minute sync Tuesday to confirm volume projections and transport preference (S3 vs SFTP)?

Thanks,
Mateo
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

---
Attachments: redwood_audit_export_proposal_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:11:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Auditline export: SLA for slices & incremental handoff

Mateo — quick internal note before we send the formal RFP response. Forwarded for context: see Sara's asks and your draft.

On the technical items:
- For tamper evidence, recommend we offer two validation levels: 
   * Standard: HMAC-SHA256 manifest + per-file SHA256 checksums (no signing key rotation SLA).
   * High-assurance: COSE signing using customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) + signed timeline (rotating key IDs).
- Transport: S3 presigned URL is simpler operationally; for SFTP we should call out throughput limitations and potential delays from queued transfers (hence the 72h SLA).
- Bulk handoff: add an option to produce an append-only compressed ledger (NDJSON blocks) with index slices to support efficient partial restore. That differentiates us from simple snapshot dumps.

Action items I suggest we include in the formal reply:
- Offer both 24h and 48h S3 SLAs as contract options tied to committed throughput.
- Include sample verification script and short runbook for chain-of-custody.
- Call out retention window enforcement and legal hold handling (we'll surface retention exceptions API).

I'll draft a one-page tech appendix and share by EOD for your review. If Sara wants the COSE signing option we’ll loop Security for KMS integration notes.

—Priyom
Principal, Platform Reliability
priyom_das@redwood.ai

Hi Mateo / Priyom — this looks good and thorough, thanks. A few clarifications from our side before the sync: 

- We'll elect the S3 presigned delivery path. Can you confirm you support 30-day presigned URLs and whether you provide automatic retrying/publish if the initial push fails?
- For high-assurance signing (COSE), we want to understand key custody: will Redwood sign with a Redwood-managed KMS and supply verification keys, or can we provide our own KMS key ARN?
- On the bulk snapshot estimate: our rough volume estimate is ~1.8TB of auditline data with redaction applied. If you can confirm the 3–7 day band for that range that will help procurement scoring.

If those answers look OK we can take the one-pager and mark the RFP as satisfied for the export section; sync Tuesday at 11:00am ET works for us.

Best,
Sara
